nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean energy|Wind turbines|Wind turbines and bird conservation_qna_000
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: What are some common predators of Wheatear chicks mentioned in the study?
nodes.answer: Common predators of Wheatear chicks mentioned in the study include mustelids such as stoats, weasels, and badgers.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean energy|Wind turbines|Wind turbines and bird conservation_qna_001
nodes.label: Taxonomy
nodes.question: When are Wheatears present in their breeding areas?
nodes.answer: Wheatears are present between May and September, with most breeding birds arriving at the end of April or early May.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean energy|Wind turbines|Wind turbines and bird conservation_qna_002
nodes.label: Strategy
nodes.question: How many broods do Wheatears typically have in the Alps?
nodes.answer: In the Alps, Wheatears typically have only one brood, but they may attempt to renest in the event of failure.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean energy|Wind turbines|Wind turbines and bird conservation_qna_003
nodes.label: Facts
nodes.question: What are the names of the two reference sites used to compare bird communities?
nodes.answer: The two reference sites are La Martinica in the North and Santuario Bosque de Niebla in the Southwest.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean energy|Wind turbines|Wind turbines and bird conservation_qna_004
nodes.label: Ecology
nodes.question: What impact did the onset of spring have on the breeding period of the Northern Wheatear?
nodes.answer: There was a delay in the breeding period in the year with a late spring onset.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean energy|Wind turbines|Wind turbines and bird conservation_qna_005
nodes.label: Ecology
nodes.question: What ecological factors did the Northern Wheatear prefer when selecting a breeding site?
nodes.answer: The Northern Wheatear preferred south-exposed productive pastures on gentle slopes, interspersed with non-vegetated ground and human-made rockpiles, and avoided shrubby or north-exposed areas as well as the vicinity of conspecific nests.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean energy|Wind turbines|Wind turbines and bird conservation_qna_006
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: What ecological factors influenced the nest site selection of the Northern Wheatear?
nodes.answer: The birds preferred south-facing, productive meadows on gently sloping hills, interspersed with vegetation-free areas and human-made stone heaps.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean energy|Wind turbines|Wind turbines and bird conservation_qna_007
nodes.label: Facts
nodes.question: Over how many breeding seasons were the nest sites of the Northern Wheatear studied?
nodes.answer: The nest sites of the Northern Wheatear were studied over four breeding seasons.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean energy|Wind turbines|Wind turbines and bird conservation_qna_008
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: What factors influence nest site selection and breeding success in the Northern Wheatear?
nodes.answer: Environmental predictors, as well as social factors like intra-specific competition and predation, influence nest site selection and breeding success in the Northern Wheatear.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean energy|Wind turbines|Wind turbines and bird conservation_qna_009
nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: How do adults Northern Wheatears behave in their breeding region?
nodes.answer: Adults usually use the same area throughout their presence in the breeding region.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean energy|Wind turbines|Wind turbines and bird conservation_qna_010
nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: What factor limits nest site availability in lowland breeding grounds for Northern Wheatears?
nodes.answer: The availability of nest sites is a limiting factor at lowland breeding grounds.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean energy|Wind turbines|Wind turbines and bird conservation_qna_011
nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: Where do Northern Wheatears typically nest in the Alps?
nodes.answer: Northern Wheatears typically nest under stones, in burrows, rockpiles, or walls in the Alps.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean energy|Wind turbines|Wind turbines and bird conservation_qna_012
nodes.label: Facts
nodes.question: How many pairs of Northern Wheatears were estimated to inhabit the study area?
nodes.answer: The study area harbored more than 100 pairs of Northern Wheatears, with a density of over 15 pairs per square kilometer.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean energy|Wind turbines|Wind turbines and bird conservation_qna_013
nodes.label: Facts
nodes.question: What percentage of nests of the northern lapwing were found in wetlands and summer crops?
nodes.answer: 94% of the nests were found in wetlands and summer crops.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean energy|Wind turbines|Wind turbines and bird conservation_qna_014
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: How have changes in agri-environmental management policies in Europe affected the northern lapwing?
nodes.answer: Changes in agri-environmental management policies have led to lower reproductive success rates and a marked decline in the northern lapwing population in Europe.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean energy|Wind turbines|Wind turbines and bird conservation_qna_015
nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: What were the two songbird species studied in relation to anthropogenic land use?
nodes.answer: The two songbird species studied were the Small Ground Finch (Geospiza fuliginosa) and the Galapagos Yellow Warbler (Setophaga petechia aureola).
